topic: Population identification of innovation-atomic causal units in grouped additive-noise models

open_problems.open_problem: Does every smooth positive law with two admissible innovation-atomic grouped additive-noise representations have comparable coordinate partitions, hence one unique refinement-minimal partition and one coordinate-labelled block DAG?

source_refs.claim: The GANM identifiability theorem treats a supplied partition; it does not compare different coordinate partitions of one law.
source_refs.author: Konstantin Göbler, Tobias Windisch, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: The paper develops fixed micro-to-group graphical relations and identifies joint learning of a partition and group graph as a challenging future direction.
source_refs.author: Jonas Wahl, Urmi Ninad, Jakob Runge

source_refs.claim: Irreducibility yields uniqueness of linear factorizations into independent subspaces, showing that atomic blocks can identify unknown block sizes in a noncausal linear analogue.
source_refs.author: Harold W. Gutch, Fabian J. Theis

source_refs.excerpt: whose images have no full opposite-arrow fiber, while each same-arrow fiber is a single G_m-orbit

open_problems.why_unsolved: Göbler–Windisch–Drton identify the DAG only after the vector groups are fixed. Ordinary independent-subspace irreducibility suggests a finest partition, but a GANM crossing must also preserve additive mechanisms, acyclicity, innovation independence, causal minimality, and conditioned edge restrictions. Residualizing one representation can mix several cells of the other, so the empty-DAG common-refinement argument does not supply a common admissible refinement. The prior LiNGAM proposal's full-fiber comparison is transferable only after replacing its cumulant fiber with a common-nondescendant conditional-density fiber; the first missing step is to prove that this conditioning does not select coordinates from a correlated alternative innovation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A population theorem proving that any two admissible representations of the same law have identical refinement-minimal coordinate partitions and identical labelled block DAGs, or a smallest smooth positive atomic crossing counterexample satisfying causal minimality and every edgewise Condition-1 clause.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from vector-valued causal units to population order identification and then graph recovery, while making the partition itself the missing identified object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific variables arrive in meaningful groups -> fixed-group GANMs orient and prune relations between those groups -> when the groups are not supplied, the observational law must first identify a unique atomic partition

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose competing independent-subspace factorizations into irreducible components and prove uniqueness up to the declared indeterminacies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Innovation atomicity is the nonlinear causal analogue of irreducibility, and the desired conclusion is likewise uniqueness of unknown block sizes and membership.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce a multivariate DAG disagreement to a bivariate additive-noise contradiction after conditioning on a carefully chosen nondescendant set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved crossing step requires exactly such a graphical reduction, but with overlap cells rather than scalar vertices.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate dHSIC and use its permutation or bootstrap limit theory to test joint independence of candidate innovations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the unique population partition is characterized, recovery requires simultaneous tests of the joint independence constraints defining its block innovations.

open_problems.open_problem: Classify the smooth-positive three-coordinate crossing between partitions {1,2}|{3} and {1,3}|{2}, proving that the two additive-noise factorizations force a directional split of a bivariate innovation or an explicitly characterized reversible exception.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives the scalar log-density differential obstruction to additive-noise representations in both directions.
source_refs.author: Patrik O. Hoyer, Dominik Janzing, Joris M. Mooij, Jonas Peters, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: The paper classifies exceptional bivariate post-nonlinear families admitting models in both directions, with additive-noise models as a special case.
source_refs.author: Kun Zhang, Aapo Hyvärinen

source_refs.excerpt: the arbitrary-m full-fiber opposite-arrow compatibility locus

open_problems.why_unsolved: Equating the two conditional densities gives a translation-family equation whose parameters vary with the shared coordinate. Local differentiation must stay within C3 regularity, so a proof cannot silently use fourth derivatives, and a chartwise translate conclusion is insufficient until null charts and overlaps are globalized. The Gaussian branch also needs exact bookkeeping: a nondegenerate multivariate Gaussian innovation is non-atomic because every coordinate split has linear ANMs, whereas scalar Gaussian innovations are vacuously atomic and linear-Gaussian edges can remain reversible. The prior compatibility-fiber method changes at its first step from polynomial cumulant equations to a C3 log-density functional equation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A positive-C3 rigidity lemma proving that every solution of the two crossing factorization equations either yields an almost-everywhere directional ANM split of one bivariate innovation that globalizes to the full support, or belongs to a completely stated exceptional family, plus a verified example if that family can remain innovation-atomic and satisfy Condition 1.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its use of a minimal local ambiguity, an explicit reversible-family analysis, and a graph-level consequence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ANM asymmetry identifies a scalar direction -> a multivariate graph disagreement can be localized by conditioning -> a crossing of unknown blocks requires a new three-coordinate rigidity lemma

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate competing log-density factorizations to derive and solve a translation-family obstruction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired crossing lemma is the overlap-conditioned, vector-innovation version of the same two-factorization equation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the vector Condition-1 differential nonidentity edgewise after a nondescendant-conditioning reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The lemma must end in exactly the fixed-group contradiction that this paper uses, while justifying the conditioning under crossed groups.

open_problems.open_problem: Which of innovation atomicity, causal minimality, smooth positivity, and the individual Göbler Condition-1 clauses are necessary for unique atomic-partition and labelled-DAG recovery, and which admit strictly weaker replacements?

source_refs.claim: The scalar theory ties causal minimality to nonconstant parent mechanisms and exhibits reversible additive-noise families that defeat labelled orientation.
source_refs.author: Jonas Peters, Joris M. Mooij, Dominik Janzing, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: Conditional-variance restrictions identify broad ANM classes under assumptions different from the standard differential asymmetry condition.
source_refs.author: Gunwoong Park

source_refs.claim: The grouped theorem assumes smooth positive block densities, causal minimality, and edgewise vector Condition 1 as sufficient conditions, without a necessity classification for unknown partitions.
source_refs.author: Konstantin Göbler, Tobias Windisch, Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dropping minimality trivially permits null-edge changes, and a non-atomic innovation suggests a strict refinement, but sharp converses must preserve every other assumption and produce two same-law representations that are themselves refinement-minimal when the conclusion demands it. Failure of one Condition-1 clause may be replaceable by conditional-variance asymmetry rather than causing nonidentification. Positivity and C3 may support intersection and differential arguments without being intrinsically necessary. The BACKSHIFT prior supplies the transferable standard—construct a legal same-class ambiguity at the threshold—but its first proof step must be replaced by a smallest-coordinate GANM pair with all untouched assumptions checked explicitly.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite assumption-indexed theorem suite that, for each assumption or Condition-1 clause, gives either an explicit smooth positive same-law pair with distinct minimal partitions or labelled DAGs satisfying all remaining assumptions, or a theorem replacing that assumption by a stated weaker necessary-and-sufficient condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its organization around a classified atlas of reversible exceptions is the right model for distinguishing necessary restrictions from convenient sufficient ones.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Directional asymmetry usually identifies ANMs -> special functional-distribution pairs remain reversible -> classifying those exceptions reveals the exact boundary of grouped partition-and-DAG identification

method_exemplars.technique: Use minimal-subgraph arguments and explicit reversible models to isolate which assumption protects which graph conclusion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired suite must separately diagnose null edges, reversible edges, and support regularity rather than bundle them into one sufficient condition.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace log-density differential asymmetry by ordered conditional-variance comparisons and prove population order recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete candidate weaker replacement when a Göbler differential clause fails but the model may remain identifiable.

open_problems.open_problem: Can admissibility, innovation atomicity, and uniqueness of the minimal grouped-ANM partition be certified by finitely many observable derivative, conditional-variance, or residual-independence quantities in a stated finite-dimensional model class?

source_refs.claim: SCORE turns score-function derivatives into population leaf criteria and a scalable estimator for fixed scalar nonlinear Gaussian ANMs.
source_refs.author: Paul Rolland, Volkan Cevher, Matthäus Kleindessner, Chris Russell, Dominik Janzing, Bernhard Schölkopf, Francesco Locatello

source_refs.claim: Characteristic-kernel dHSIC is zero exactly at joint independence and has valid consistent permutation and bootstrap tests.
source_refs.author: Niklas Pfister, Peter Bühlmann, Bernhard Schölkopf, Jonas Peters

source_refs.claim: The grouped model uses continuum-valued differential restrictions and residual-independence procedures for a supplied partition, not a finite sound-and-complete unknown-partition certificate.
source_refs.author: Konstantin Göbler, Tobias Windisch, Mathias Drton

source_refs.excerpt: the graph of s to Psi(s) is a finite union of semialgebraic graphs

open_problems.why_unsolved: The coordinate dimension makes candidate partitions finite, but each candidate's model membership is still infinite-dimensional: Condition 1 is a functional nonidentity and atomicity quantifies over all coordinate splits and both internal directions. A finite jet can match local identities without proving global residual independence, normalization, or absence of a distant split. The prior semialgebraic-fiber construction transfers only after a new finite-jet completeness theorem; quantifier elimination cannot supply that missing analytic step. Targeted searches found derivative criteria for fixed scalar ANMs and independence tests, but no finite sound-and-complete certificate for unknown innovation-atomic GANM partitions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a fixed-dimension theorem giving a finite list of observable equalities and strict inequalities equivalent to existence and uniqueness of an atomic GANM representation within a named finite-dimensional class, together with consistent estimators and a joint recovery limit law, or an impossibility theorem producing laws with identical prescribed finite certificates but different atomic partitions.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its clean separation between population identification, order learning, edge pruning, and empirical evaluation, adding partition certification as the first rung.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Vector ANM asymmetry identifies a DAG when groups are known -> unknown groups require observable atomicity and admissibility checks -> finite certificates with recovery guarantees turn population uniqueness into a usable procedure

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate score Jacobians, prove a population zero-pattern criterion, and control the plug-in errors used by iterative graph recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how differential ANM identities can become finite observable statistics with a recovery theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use characteristic-kernel joint-independence functionals with permutation or bootstrap calibration and fixed-alternative consistency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Candidate block innovations are defined by joint independence, so this supplies the limit theory needed after regression residualization.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover unknown irreducible subspace dimensions from uniqueness of the finest linear independent decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest finite-dimensional analogue in which atomic blocks, rather than prespecified group sizes, determine the partition.

open_problems.open_problem: Do the population-oracle versions of Niu's CIC search and Rajpal's variational cluster-DAG learner target the same partition-and-graph equivalence class, or is there a smooth positive innovation-atomic GANM lying in exactly one method's recovery domain?

source_refs.claim: CIC combines information-theoretic interaction terms with an MDL penalty and a search strategy for cluster causal diagrams; its target is not an atomic GANM partition theorem.
source_refs.author: Xueyan Niu, Xiaoyun Li, Ping Li

source_refs.claim: The method places categorical and Bernoulli variational distributions over latent clusters and graph edges and optimizes variational lower bounds, with empirical rather than population target-uniqueness guarantees.
source_refs.author: Avni Rajpal, Anubhav Kumar, Rishabh Karnad, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, P. K. Srijith

source_refs.excerpt: Q_{j,S}(P)=0 if and only if j is a leaf of G[S]

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two algorithms optimize different objects: CIC is an information-theoretic MDL score with combinatorial search, while Rajpal uses variational distributions over assignments and edges with Monte Carlo optimization. Their cluster semantics and graph equivalence classes must first be aligned with the coordinate-labelled atomic GANM target. Generic empirical success is not an oracle equivalence theorem, and an ELBO optimum need not coincide with a CIC optimum. The prior SCORE certificate suggests an exact-zero population comparison, but its first step must change from scalar leaf residualization to a blockwise certificate that remains valid while cluster membership is itself unknown.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Formal definitions of both exact-population procedures followed by either a theorem that their global optima equal the unique atomic GANM partition and labelled DAG under one explicit common assumption set, or a fully specified positive-C3 atomic GANM for which exactly one population objective returns that target.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation of simultaneous cluster and C-DAG search supplies the destination problem, but the new work must sharpen the target to innovation-atomic GANM units.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scalar-variable DAGs miss polyadic interactions -> cluster causal diagrams make groups first-class causal objects -> simultaneous learning needs a population target and a proof that competing objectives recover the same atomic units

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize population causal order by vector residual asymmetry and recover edges by multivariate residual goodness-of-fit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once an objective proposes a partition, this is the closest population criterion for checking that its labelled group DAG is the GANM target.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate joint-independence tests for the residual blocks generated by each candidate clustering.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A statistical recovery rung needs an inferential bridge from either population objective to verifiable independence of the selected innovations.

open_problems.open_problem: Are the 19 process-defined groups in the Bosch assembly-line analysis refinement-minimal innovation-atomic causal units, or do admissible within-process refinements or cross-process regroupings fit the observed law equally well?

source_refs.claim: The application treats 19 manufacturing-process groups as supplied inputs and evaluates a learned group DAG using only partial production-order knowledge.
source_refs.author: Konstantin Göbler, Tobias Windisch, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: causalAssembly fits a semisynthetic generator to real production measurements under a partially physics-informed graph because complete causal ground truth is unavailable.
source_refs.author: Konstantin Göbler, Tobias Windisch, Mathias Drton, Tim Pychynski, Martin Roth, Steffen Sonntag

source_refs.excerpt: exhausts all 24 common orders, every realizable full-ledger sign cell, and all exact support indices
claimed exhaustive p=4 certificate contained only one explicit row and one intensional protocol record

open_problems.why_unsolved: The 19 groups encode engineering processes, not units recovered from the observational distribution. The real-data study lacks full graph ground truth, and a semisynthetic generator that is Markov to a chosen graph cannot independently validate uniqueness of that graph or grouping. No located study tests whether a multivariate process residual has an internal directional ANM or whether a crossing grouping remains admissible. The rejected prior audit shows the concrete certification risk: a protocol and one example row do not establish exhaustive coverage. Data access may limit an empirical answer, so the audit must distinguish checked population or semisynthetic claims from unresolved real-data hypotheses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rerunnable 19-process ledger encoding the available structural equations or fitted conditional laws, enumerating all credible within-process splits and selected crossings, recording atomicity and Condition-1 tests with multiplicity-aware uncertainty, and separately reporting the population outputs of the Göbler, Niu, and Rajpal procedures without treating process labels as identified ground truth.

writing_exemplar.why: Its careful separation of real measurements, partial physical knowledge, fitted mechanisms, privacy constraints, and semisynthetic ground truth is the right reporting standard.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real industrial data have incomplete causal ground truth -> physics-informed semisynthetic mechanisms enable controlled benchmarks -> the published 19-group partition still requires a separate atomicity and refinement audit

method_exemplars.technique: Fit multivariate block mechanisms, test residual independence, recover a group order, and prune the graph under vector ANM restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The audit asks whether the same pipeline remains stable when its supplied 19-group partition is replaced by candidate refinements and crossings.

method_exemplars.technique: Use permutation or bootstrap dHSIC tests for joint independence of cross-fitted candidate innovation blocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The empirical atomicity claim requires uncertainty-aware residual-independence tests across many proposed partitions.

literature_map:
1. Hoyer et al. (NeurIPS 2008) derive the scalar ANM log-density obstruction.
2. Zhang and Hyvärinen (UAI 2009) classify reversible post-nonlinear families, including ANM exceptions.
3. Peters et al. (JMLR 2014) lift local conditioned ANM asymmetry to scalar DAG identification.
4. Gutch and Theis (JMVA 2012) identify unknown irreducible independent subspaces in a linear noncausal analogue.
5. Parviainen and Kaski (IJAR 2017) show that groupwise conditional independences alone do not orient supplied groups.
6. Pfister et al. (JRSS B 2018) give dHSIC's joint-independence characterization and calibrated tests.
7. Park (JMLR 2020) supplies conditional-variance ANM identification under a different restriction family.
8. Niu, Li, and Li (IJCAI 2022) use CIC plus MDL search to learn C-DAG clusters and edges jointly.
9. Rolland et al. (ICML 2022) turn score-Jacobian identities into fixed-scalar ANM recovery.
10. Wahl, Ninad, and Runge (AAAI 2023; JCI 2024) study supplied vector groups and explicitly flag joint partition-graph learning.
11. Morioka and Hyvärinen (ICML 2024) identify latent causal representations under supplied grouping assumptions, a different target.
12. Göbler et al. (CLeaR 2024) provide causalAssembly with partial physical and semisynthetic ground truth.
13. Göbler, Windisch, and Drton (UAI 2025) prove fixed-partition GANM DAG identification under vector Condition 1.
14. Rajpal et al. (arXiv 2026) jointly learn latent clusters and graph edges variationally, without a population target-uniqueness theorem.
15. Across these papers, the live tension is fixed-group DAG identifiability versus unknown-group algorithms without a theorem excluding atomic crossing partitions.
prior_proposal_map:
1. The accepted LiNGAM full-fiber run was mined for representation-fiber separation and its warning about undeclared symmetries.
2. Its open exceptional-locus question supplies a technique analogue for the three-coordinate crossing classification.
3. The downgraded SCORE run supplies exact-zero leaf certificates as a template for population algorithm comparison.
4. The active robust-BACKSHIFT run supplies the strongest prior template for legal same-class sharp converses.
5. The downgraded partial-difference run was mined for finite semialgebraic branch certification.
6. Its rejected four-vertex angle and bank README expose the failure mode of claiming an exhaustive audit from an intensional protocol.
7. No prior Niu, Rajpal, or Bosch-specific proof artifact was found; those directions rely primarily on the web papers and only borrow prior certification techniques.
